Report_ID: CAPS-IV total score — omnibus Time × Treatment interaction at treatment end (active 1-Hz and 10-Hz vs sham)
Title: A Randomized Sham-controlled Trial of 1-Hz and 10-Hz Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS) of the Right Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex in Civilian Post-traumatic Stress Disorder
Author: Leong, Chan, Ong, Zwicker, Willan, Lam, McGirr
Comment: Omnibus 3-arm interaction F test; no group means attached to this row (the arm-level means are recorded in the two arm-specific rows). No effect size (eta-squared or similar) reported by the paper for this interaction, so effect_size fields left empty. This row duplicates the construct of the arm-level rows and should not be pooled in addition to them.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Active rTMS right DLPFC (1-Hz n = 11 and 10-Hz n = 9)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); ANOVA excluded: comparison_type='mixed' is not between-group
Participant type: civilian adults aged 19-70 with primary non-combat-related DSM-IV PTSD
Recruitment source: Psychiatry outpatient and community programs of Vancouver Coastal Health
Outcome measurement: F test for the Time × Treatment interaction across the three arms (1-Hz, 10-Hz, sham) in the mixed model
Outcome variable: CAPS-IV total score — omnibus Time × Treatment interaction at treatment end (active 1-Hz and 10-Hz vs sham)

Report_ID: Change from baseline in CAPS-5 total score at week 5 (immediately after treatment course) — intention-to-treat analysis
Title: Deep Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation Combined With Brief Exposure for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder: A Prospective Multisite Randomized Trial
Author: Isserles M, Tendler A, Roth Y, et al.
Comment: Values are ADJUSTED mean improvements (i.e. reductions) from baseline with 95% CIs from the trial's model-based analysis; no SDs or SEs of change are reported, and no between-group difference estimate/CI is given, so M_diff/SE_diff were left empty. Note the sign convention: larger value = greater symptom reduction (opposite orientation to raw severity), so sham improved MORE than active dTMS. Per-arm n used are the randomised/safety (ITT) set sizes (dTMS 60, sham 65) from Table 1; exact numbers contributing at week 5 are not stated in the text. Results come from a preplanned interim analysis (per-protocol set n=109; 91 reached the week-5 end point). Per-protocol figures for the same time point were 16.32 (12.70–19.94) dTMS vs 20.52 (17.42–23.63) sham, p = .027.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('SDI + active deep TMS (H7 coil, 18 Hz, mPFC/ACC)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Design Type: randomized double-blind sham-controlled parallel-group multicenter trial
Participant type: adult outpatients (22–68 years) meeting DSM-5 criteria for PTSD with CAPS-5 ≥ 25
Recruitment source: public advertisements and physician referrals at 15 clinical centers
Outcome measurement: Adjusted mean improvement (points of CAPS-5 reduction) with 95% CI, mixed-model/adjusted analysis
Outcome variable: Change from baseline in CAPS-5 total score at week 5 (immediately after treatment course) — intention-to-treat analysis
outcome_units: CAPS-5 total score points (improvement from baseline)

Report_ID: PTSD symptom severity (CAPS total score) at posttreatment
Title: A sham controlled study of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation for posttraumatic stress disorder
Author: Watts BV, Landon B, Groft A, Young-Xu Y
Comment: Paper reports only baseline and posttreatment means (SD) per arm, not change scores or SDs of change. Baseline CAPS: sham 72.3 (12.2), active rTMS 81.6 (9.5); posttreatment values recorded in group_1_mean/group_2_mean. Mean change can be derived downstream as post minus baseline (sham -10.6; rTMS -27.7) with change SD derived assuming r=0.5. M_diff left empty to avoid conflating the posttreatment difference with the planned change-score difference. The reported P value is from a Mann-Whitney test; no effect size or CI reported.
Participant type: adult veterans with primary PTSD diagnosis (SCID) and CAPS > 50
Recruitment source: Behavioral Sciences Service Line, White River Junction Veterans Affairs Medical Center, Vermont
Outcome measurement: Mean (SD) CAPS total score per arm at baseline and immediately posttreatment; between-group comparison by Mann-Whitney test
Outcome variable: PTSD symptom severity (CAPS total score) at posttreatment

Report_ID: Total-CAPS score change from baseline to week 5
Title: Effectiveness of Deep Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation Combined with a Brief Exposure Procedure in Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder - A Pilot Study
Author: Isserles et al.
Comment: Values are mean ± STANDARD ERROR of the IMPROVEMENT (symptom reduction), not of raw post-treatment severity: a larger positive value means greater symptom reduction, i.e. the sign is reversed relative to a post-minus-baseline change score. SE recorded in the _se fields (paper states "mean SE"). The 'treatment criterion' population (N=26, per-arm n=9/8/9) was used because the ITT column (N=30) does not report per-arm Ns. Three-arm trial: the second active arm (NOEX-STIM, n=8) is reported in additional_group_ns rather than combined, because combining arm means/SDs was not reported by the paper. Between-group group*time interaction was NOT significant (P=0.12); p_value recorded is the pre-planned EXP-STIM vs EXP-SHAM Fisher's PLSD contrast (P=0.08).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('EXP-STIM — active DTMS (mPFC, 20 Hz, 1680 pulses at 120% MT, 12 sessions) after script-driven imagery of the traumatic event') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); treatment SD derived from its reported SE (SD = SE * sqrt(n)); control SD derived from its reported SE (SD = SE * sqrt(n)); N-INCONSISTENCY: n_control(9) + n_treatment(9) = 18 ≠ n_total(26) — verify per-group Ns
Design Type: randomized double-blind sham-controlled parallel-group pilot trial
Recruitment source: Newspaper ads and referrals from medical faculties/personnel; Dept of Psychiatry, Hadassah-Hebrew University Medical Center, Jerusalem
Outcome measurement: Mean ± SE improvement in Total-CAPS during treatment, 'treatment criterion' population (N=26, patients who received at least 8 treatment sessions)
Outcome variable: Total-CAPS score change from baseline to week 5
additional_group_ns: Second active arm NOEX-STIM (active DTMS after positive/non-traumatic script), n=8, Total-CAPS improvement 9.9 ± 5.9 (mean ± SE) — not included in the two extracted arms; ITT (N=30) column improvements: EXP-STIM 24.3 ± 7.4, NOEX-STIM 7.9 ± 4.8, EXP-SHAM 9.1 ± 5.1 (per-arm ITT Ns not reported)
outcome_units: CAPS points (improvement; higher value = greater symptom reduction)

Report_ID: CAPS-5 PTSD symptom severity at end of 2-week double-blind phase (active iTBS vs sham iTBS)
Title: Theta Burst Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
Author: Philip NS, Barredo J, Aiken E, Larson V, Jones RN, Shea MT, Greenberg BD, van 't Wout-Frank M
Comment: Table 2a column headers are mis-aligned in the extracted text; the first Mean/SD pair is Sham baseline (47.4, 10.6) and the second is Sham two-weeks (39.4, 13.8), followed by Active baseline (47.9, 10.0) and Active two-weeks (38.6, 11.4) — consistent with Table 1 baseline values. Only post-treatment means/SDs are entered in the group fields; baseline means/SDs (sham 47.4±10.6; active 47.9±10.0, n=25 each) are available for deriving change scores with r=0.5. Reported Cohen's d is standardized to a pooled BASELINE SD, so it is not identical to a change-score SMD. ITT n=25 per group with multiple imputation (20 imputations).
Recruitment source: Providence VA Medical Center, May 2016 - December 2017
Outcome measurement: CAPS-5 total score (higher = worse PTSD); two-week post-treatment mean and SD per arm, with baseline mean and SD also reported
Outcome variable: CAPS-5 PTSD symptom severity at end of 2-week double-blind phase (active iTBS vs sham iTBS)

Report_ID: PTSD symptom severity (CAPS) reduction from baseline at session 5
Title: Exposure Therapy and Simultaneous Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation: A Controlled Pilot Trial for the Treatment of Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
Author: Fryml et al.
Comment: Only PERCENTAGE reductions with 90% CIs are reported; no post-treatment means or SDs, so mean change, SD of change, and an SMD cannot be computed. Baseline CAPS (Table 2) was 84 ± 25.7 (active, n=5) and 73 ± 28.9 (control, n=3), but the "±" is not labelled as SD or SE in the table. The paper's own CI for the active group (18.5–53.5) does not contain its point estimate (55%), i.e. the reported numbers are internally inconsistent as printed. Difference described as a nonsignificant trend; no test statistic or p-value reported for CAPS. Both arms also received prolonged exposure therapy as a co-intervention. No values were computed or imputed.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Active rTMS (left or right prefrontal, 10 Hz, 120% MT) + prolonged exposure therapy') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Participant type: OIF/OEF military veterans aged 21–50 with war-related PTSD
Recruitment source: Ralph H. Johnson Veterans Administration Medical Center, Charleston, SC
Outcome measurement: Percentage reduction in CAPS total score from baseline (with 90% confidence intervals); baseline CAPS means reported in Table 2
Outcome variable: PTSD symptom severity (CAPS) reduction from baseline at session 5
